title: Magnetic Separator

introduction.definition: A wet drum magnetic separator recovers magnetic particles such as magnetite from a slurry. A non-magnetic stainless drum turns around a stationary permanent-magnet arc. Magnetic particles are attracted to the drum surface, carried out of the slurry and released into the concentrate launder where the field ends; non-magnetic particles flow on to tailings.
key_points: Field typically ~ 0.1–0.3 T at drum surface (low intensity)

classification.type: Wet drum, permanent magnet, concurrent tank

introduction.summary: A wet drum magnetic separator recovers magnetic particles (for example magnetite) from a slurry. A non-magnetic drum rotates around a stationary magnet arc; magnetic particles are attracted to the drum, carried out of the slurry and dropped into the concentrate launder, while non-magnetic material flows to tailings.

magnetic_field.title: Magnetic field round the lower drum
magnetic_field.description: The stationary magnet arc creates a strong field (typically ~ 0.1–0.3 T at the drum surface for magnetite recovery) only over the lower part of the drum. Magnetic particles are pulled onto the rotating shell, carried out of the slurry and released where the field ends; non-magnetic particles stay in the slurry and leave as tailings.

video_tutorials.title: Magnetic Separator — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Magnetic Separator.
A wet drum magnetic separator recovers magnetic particles such as magnetite from a slurry.
A non-magnetic stainless drum turns around a stationary permanent-magnet arc.
Magnetic particles are attracted to the drum surface, carried out of the slurry and released into the concentrate launder where the field ends; non-magnetic particles flow on to tailings.
Typical applications include magnetite recovery in iron-ore concentrators; dense-medium recovery in coal washing; removal of iron from minerals.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Tank, Feed Box & Concentrate Launder, Rotating Non-Magnetic Stainless Drum, Drum Wear Strips (show the drum rotation).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Magnetic Separator works.
Slurry enters the feed box.
The magnet arc creates a field round the lower drum.
Magnetic particles stick to the turning drum.
They are released into the concentrate launder.
Non-magnetic particles leave as tailings.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The stationary magnet arc creates a strong field (typically ~ 0.1–0.3 T at the drum surface for magnetite recovery) only over the lower part of the drum.

video_tutorials.title: Magnetic Separator — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Magnetic Separator.
Check slurry level and drum surface.
Measure field strength; inspect wear liner.
Replace drum shell/liners.
Watch for loss of magnetics to tailings: low recovery. Common cause: field weakening, high slurry velocity.
Watch for drum wear: holes in shell. Common cause: abrasion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
